span: this is a fit case to exercise powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and to quash the impugned criminal proceedings
why: Court itself applies s.482 to quash the criminal proceedings in the case.

span: Section 482 CrPC saves the inherent power of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Code, or to prevent abuse of the process of any court
why: Extract from the court's own earlier decision (Vineet Kumar) on the scope of s.482; adoption for the present case is not stated in the passage.

span: if the basic ingredients of the offence alleged are altogether absent, the criminal proceedings may be quashed under Section 482 of CrPC
why: Headnote: quashing is available when ingredients are absent but the power must not stifle legitimate prosecution; in this case the High Court's refusal to quash was upheld.

span: Whether the High Court would be justified in granting stay of further investigation pending the proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
why: Concerns interim stay of investigation during a quashing petition, not the power to quash itself.

span: the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and with circumspection and that too in the rarest of rare cases
why: Court says the Bhajan Lal precautionary principles remain good law: the power exists but is for the rarest cases; no outcome on a specific FIR in this passage.

span: The court should be guarded in the use of its extraordinary jurisdiction to quash an FIR or criminal proceeding
why: Court says s.482 powers are wide but must be used with caution when quashing an FIR; states the standard without deciding a specific FIR here.

span: in exercise of its inherent powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and/or Article 226 of the Constitution of India, may quash the FIR/complaint/criminal proceedings
why: Court says the High Court may quash only in exceptional cases of abuse and should be slow at the initial stage; both the power and the restraint are stated.
